topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the core learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Determinants of cancer risk: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer causation by evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents drive oncogenesis, illustrating these mechanisms in detail through the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how specific physical and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation, induce oxidative stress, and cause direct DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and host susceptibility factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumour promotion mechanisms within the two-stage model of carcinogenesis alongside developmental and physiological host susceptibility factors.

topics.label: Approaches for identifying carcinogens and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic recaps the major themes of environmental cancer causation and closes the lecture.
